title: He washed feet… while others chased fire.
paragraphs: He washed feet… while others chased fire.

No spotlight.
No applause.
Just water… and a towel.
But here’s what most people miss—

Stephanas wasn’t weak.
He was dangerously devoted.
And that kind of life exposes something in us.

We don’t mind serving—
as long as we’re seen.

We don’t mind helping—
as long as it’s honored.

We don’t mind sacrifice—
as long as it trends.
That’s where pride starts to choke.

Some of us don’t struggle with laziness.
We struggle with the need to be noticed.

We want to be used by God…
but we also want to be recognized by people.
And that is where the tension begins.
Because the Kingdom of Jesus doesn’t run on visibility.
Stephanas walks into Scripture almost unnoticed.

No dramatic entrance.
No thunder from heaven.
Just this one line that hits like a hammer:
“You know that the household of Stephanas were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints.” — 1 Corinthians 16:15

Not interested.
Not occasional.
Not convenient.
That word in the original sense carries the idea of assigning oneself fully, almost like a soldier reporting for duty without being forced.
Stephanas didn’t wait to be asked.
Few want to kneel with a towel.
But the Gospel says something radically different.
“Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves.” — Philippians 2:3
That’s the DNA of Christ Himself.
Because Jesus didn’t just preach humility—
“If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.” — John 13:14
This is the moment pride dies.
This is where greatness is redefined.
And here’s the deeper truth most people avoid:

It hides in comparison.
In silent resentment.
In the need for validation.
but secretly wonder if it’s worth it.
And this is where the Gospel explodes with clarity.
Because you and I don’t just need better attitudes.
Pride isn’t fixed by trying harder.
Jesus didn’t come to create impressive people.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
While we were still wrapped in pride.
And through His death and resurrection—
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
Stephanas didn’t earn grace by serving.
He served because grace had already changed him.
Religion says: Serve so God will accept you.
The Gospel says: You are accepted in Christ—now you are free to serve.
So now the question is not—
“Is Jesus enough… even if no one does?”
comes from your most hidden obedience?
What if heaven is celebrating moments…

Every unseen act.
Every quiet prayer.
Every hidden sacrifice.
“Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.” — Matthew 6:4
But maybe today, this hits deeper.

“Lord, cleanse my heart.
Break my pride.
Teach me to love like You.”
Because Jesus doesn’t reject broken people.
Lay down the need to be seen.
If this stirred something in you…
